source: Daily Investment Brief Macroeconomic Dashboard + authoritative-source supplementation
sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief remains the primary dashboard layer, but automated retrieval still returns client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--'). Those placeholders are not interpreted as values. MacroMicro direct automated retrieval was not reliable in this run, so gaps are filled with Federal Reserve H.15, official ISM and current Reuters market reporting. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard readings are inputs, not trading signals. Creator/video/social claims have zero direct score weight until independently verified.
regime: Energy/refined-product inflation + rising global long-end/real yields + weakening equity breadth, while physical industrial/AI capex remains expansionary but increasingly screened for funded demand.

keyReadings.label: Spot gold
keyReadings.note: Gold fell sharply as real/nominal yields and USD rose; structural hedge thesis remains separate from tactical trend.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.interpretation: August ISM Manufacturing stayed expansionary at 54.6 with Production 58.3, but New Orders fell to 53.7 and Backlog to 51.8. Physical demand remains real, yet broad acceleration is no longer the right assumption.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.interpretation: Oil-driven inflation and hawkish Fed communication pushed September hike pricing to roughly 68%. Jobs and CPI can still change the decision, so do not treat market odds as certainty.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.interpretation: US 10Y traded near 4.80%, official Aug 31 10Y real TIPS reached 2.44%, US 30Y 5.25%, and Japan 10Y hit 3%. This is a direct valuation/funding headwind for leveraged, long-duration and pre-commercial equities.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.interpretation: Capital remains available to high-quality issuers, but rising risk-free rates and heavy AI-related issuance raise the cost of funding and make per-share cash conversion more important.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: The last verified CCC-and-lower yield reference near 14.6% plus higher real yields keeps the weakest borrowers under pressure. Treat the exact CCC level as dated until refreshed, but the direction of refinancing stress is unfavorable.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: Higher diesel/gasoline and borrowing costs reduce discretionary purchasing power. The consumer is not in collapse, but the hurdle rises for travel, housing and discretionary cyclicals.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: A 10Y near 4.8% and 30Y around 5.25% are unambiguously hostile to mortgage affordability and leveraged property activity.

channels.label: Industrial / Power Capex
channels.regime: Strong physical demand, but interconnection requests require quality screening
channels.interpretation: August ISM production and component shortages still validate the physical buildout. However, more than 700 GW of US data-centre grid requests and utility audits reveal 'ghost demand'; prefer deposit-backed projects, booked orders and customer-funded capacity over headline request pipelines.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.interpretation: ISM Prices stayed at 71.1 while diesel, fuel, freight, copper, electrical/electronic components, memory and semiconductors were reported higher. This is the strongest current macro support for scarce physical producers and the clearest margin threat for low-pricing-power users.

channels.label: Labour
channels.regime: Manufacturing employment expanding more slowly; broader jobs test pending
channels.interpretation: ISM Manufacturing Employment slowed to 51.2 while July Services Employment was 47.4. Do not front-run the upcoming US labor releases; the signal is mixed rather than a confirmed labor break.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.regime: Fragile breadth / rotation beneath headline indices
channels.interpretation: Sep 1 S&P fell 0.71%, Nasdaq 1.03%, and decliners materially outnumbered advancers while energy outperformed. The Live Desk also shows a 40/100 fragile pulse. Creator block-trade claims remain unverified and contribute zero score weight.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent settled $94.65 and WTI $90.22 after renewed US-Iran fighting. The trade is physically tight but increasingly self-limiting through demand destruction, policy response and Americas supply rerouting.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.regime: Middle-distillate scarcity remains the dominant energy-inflation channel
channels.interpretation: US diesel futures hit a 52-month high alongside refinery disruptions. Refined products remain a stronger inflation and earnings signal than crude alone.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: US feedgas advantage + global security premium
channels.interpretation: US LNG infrastructure retains strategic value as buyers diversify supply, but high global spot prices can destroy price-sensitive demand. Favor contracted/take-or-pay infrastructure over pure spot-beta.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Structural thesis intact, tactical trend under pressure
channels.interpretation: Gold fell about 2.4% to ~$4,342 as USD and real/nominal yields rose, moving below its 200-day average. Long-run fiscal/geopolitical hedge logic remains, but the immediate entry requires staging rather than chasing.
